Pt is an 82yo male w/ hx of CAD s/p CABG, HTN, CHF w/ EF 35%, AF,
   sustained VT w/ ablation & AICD. Was watching TV @ home when suddenly
   felt lightheaded/ diaphoretic, followed by his AICD firing x1. Called
   EMS & brought to EW. Was found to be in a slow VT rate 120s. EP planned
   for cardioversion (received etomidate) but was able to brake VT by
   anti-tachycardial pacing. Was Amio loaded & started on a gtt. Also
   plavix loaded, got 80 lipitor & started on heparin gtt for concerns of
   ACS. Tnsf to CCU on amio/ heparin gtts, CE x3 flat.
   EPS complete [**11-28**].  Successful ablation of one source of VT,
   unsuccessful ablation attempts at second source. ICD interrogated and
   adjustments made to ATP rate.  Pt w/ chest pain/ nausea/ vomiting at
   end of case- tx
d with 50mcg fentanyl w/ complete relief of chest pain
   and some residual nausea.   Hematoma at end of sheath pull noted and
   marked by EP fellow Dr. [**First Name (STitle) 5680**]. Later that evening, pt w/ new groin
   bleed and +AV fistula per US. Manual pressure held and Vascular surgery
   consulted- no need for intervention at this time, but continuing to
   follow.
   Arteriovenous fistula (AVF) , Procedure-related
   Assessment:
   R femoral AV fistula per US [**11-28**]. +R fem bruit. Soft
   hematoma/ecchymosis at site- within marked borders.   R DP dopplerable,
   R PT palpable. BLE equally warm to touch with baseline coloring. Pt
   denied pain/ numbness/ or any other abnormal feelings in R leg. Dsg
   this AM with very small amt new bright red blood (approx 1-2 drops).
   HCT stable 28.9 this am.
   Action:
   Vascular [**Doctor First Name 458**] following. Team notified of new blood on dsg. Dsg
   removed- no visible bleeding from sites. Pressure dsg applied. Frequent
   assessment of pedal pulses, distal circulation.
   Response:
   Stable. R groin without further bleeding..
   Plan:
   Continue to closely monitor R groin for expanding/worsening hematoma/
   fistula or s/s RLE ischemia. Recheck HCT at 17:00. Follow-up US on
   Friday [**12-1**]. Restart anticoagulation for A-fib [**12-1**] (coumadin/
   heparin gtt).
   Ventricular tachycardia, sustained
   Assessment:
   HR AV/V paced @ 70BPM with PVCs. No further runs V-tach.
   Action:
   Continues on PO lopressor and Amiodarone. Awaiting restart of IV
   heparin gtt bridge back to coumadin for hx A-fib. ICD interrogated
   yesterday as noted above.
   Response:
   Stable on current regimen.
   Plan:
   Continue to closely monitor HR/rhythm.
   Knowledge Deficit
   Assessment:
   Still intermittently refusing dosing of PO hydralazine. Concern for
   medication compliance at home- please see yesterday
s nursing note.
   Action:
   Reinforced teaching from [**11-28**].
   Response:
   Still appears skeptical re: teaching.
   Plan:
   Evaluate need for home VNA at time of DC for med compliance issues and
   BP/R groin checks. Reinforce initial teaching.

same pain again which was also associated with some nausea,
vomiting, and anorexia with focal discomfort in the
epigastrium and diffuse discomfort throughout the abdomen.

On the day prior to presentation, he progressively worsened
throughout the day; however, he did not want to come into the

patient was awake, was lying still, and appeared to be in
moderate distress.  On arrival in the Emergency Department,
it was noted that his temperature was 92.8, heart rate was
100, blood pressure was 76/45, respiratory rate was 16, and
the oxygen saturation was 98% on room air.  The cardiac
examination revealed tachycardia with a regular rhythm.  The
lungs were clear to auscultation bilaterally.  The abdomen
was distended and diffusely tender.  There was positive
guarding.  There was no rebound, and no rigidity.  The
extremities were cool and clammy with decreased capillary
refill.

fat stranding with some free fluid around the pancreas.
There was a partially distended gallbladder with an edematous
wall.

A follow-up CT was performed with contrast which showed a
shift of previously seen fluid to more dependent regions of
the abdomen.

Surgical Intensive Care Unit.  A Swan-Ganz catheter was
placed as well as arterial lines.  Aggressive resuscitation
was undertaken, and he had a follow-up CT which showed a
fluid collection down the right gutter accumulating around
the cecum.  It was elected that because of his current
condition it was likely that he had a perforated ulcer with
retroperitoneal process.

He was brought to the operating room for exploratory
laparotomy, appendectomy, complete Kocherization of the
duodenum and exploration of the lesser sac.  Please see the

continued.

the previous 24 hours and requiring less oxygen.  The patient

antibiotic regimen was continued.  He was transferred to the
floor.

passing flatus, and had bowel movements.  The patient was
afebrile over the previous evening and was continuing to
improve.  The intravenous antibiotics were continued.  A
peripherally inserted central catheter line was placed for
continuation of intravenous antibiotics.

regimen of Zosyn, tobramycin, and Flagyl.  The patient
remained afebrile and was found to be continuing to improve.

exam showed that she was afebrile with temperature of 98.6,

coronary artery lesions.

showing clean coronaries, it was felt that her chest pain was

blocker for blood pressure control.

accepted to a rehab facility where she will be discharged.

DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES:
1.  Noncardiac chest pain.
2.  Status post cardiac cath complicated by large groin

3.  Hypertension.

CONDITION ON DISCHARGE:  Good.

Y stent was placed the patient had significant bronchospasm on
exam in the PACU, believed to be due to severe COPD
exacerbation. Repeat bronchoscopy at that time showed the Y
stent was in good position. CXR was not remarkable for any new
changes.  The patient was intubated and sent to the ICU.  Repeat
bronchoscopy revealed purulent sputum consistent with
tracheobronchitis. The patient was started on vancomycin and
zosyn treatment.  The patient was extubated, but quickly failed
this largely due to anxiety, tachycardia, hypertension and
tachypnea, and was quickly re-intubated.  The paln was to
optimize his other hemodynamic parameters prior to re-attempting
extubation.  He was aggressively diuresed with lasix and
responded well. His blood pressure and heart rate were
controlled with beta blockade, verapamil and ace inhibitors.  He
continued antibiotic therapy but worsening of secretions
prevented extubation for some time.  His anxiety was eventually
controlled with standing clonazepam as well as prn haldol.  The
patient was difficult to awaken from sedation and took several
days to become responsive. This was in the setting of elevated
liver function tests and elevated ammonia. He was started on
lactulose TID and zosyn was stopped on [**2-8**] as it can cause
transaminitis and his course was nearly completed. CT head was
unremarkable and after 2-3 days the patient awakened off
sedation and became responsive to questions.

to oxygen by nasal cannula without problem.  His goal O2
saturation is approximately 90-92% given the severity of his
COPD and he was able to maintain this on nasal cannula. He was
treated with nebulizers as well as guafenesin liquid standing.
Ideally he should be on mucinex tabs 1200mg po bid, however this
cannot be crushed so we substituted with Mucinex.  He was given
aggressive chest PT and used a mechanical in-exsufflator three
times daily, which should be continued at rehab.
     He was initially on high dose IV steroids, but is currently
in the course of a prednisone taper. His current dose is 30mg po
daily and he should continue this for 4 more days, then decrease
to 20mg po daily for 5 days, then decrease to 10mg po daily for
5 days, then off.  He should be maintained on his current
singulair dose as well as standing and prn nebulizer treatments.

passes swallow evaluation and can swallow pills this should be
changed to mucinex tabs 1200mg po bid as this is ideal for his
stenting but cannot be crushed.

episode of desaturation that responded well to clonazepam as
well as suctioning.  Again, anxiety has been a recurrent problem
for his respiratory status. Should he develop desaturation or
respiratory distress consider using clonazepam or haldol as well
as suctioning.
